# Labour Fraud Analysis

A portfolio **case file**. A private labour-migration / financial-crime document corpus is run
through a deterministic anonymisation pipeline, and what ships is a 20-table **synthetic** relational
dataset — 1,472 structured rows over 512 document records — with three analysis surfaces and a
long-form narrative. The engineering deliverable is the pipeline and its gate, not the finding.

**Status: finished and frozen at last commit 2026-07-11.** 8 commits, seven inside one second and
the eighth four minutes later — [[import-finished-work-into-git]]. The README banner and
`docs/investigation.md` §5 both describe the *underlying matter* as "real, active" and
"ACTIVE — under review"; the repo itself is presented as complete.

**Publish stance — reversed 2026-07-30.** The original stance was `publish: false` on every page
for this repo, per the interview ("just keep it as it is"). The author lifted it deliberately on
2026-07-30, having been shown what the blanket held back: twelve tech and method pages that carry
nothing from the matter itself.

What the reversal does **not** change: the underlying corpus is not here, was never here, and no
page reproduces a name, an identifier or a document from it. Every value in the shipped dataset is
invented — see [[synthesise-rather-than-redact]] and [[structure-preserving-anonymisation]]. What
is now public is the *method*: how the substitution is seeded, what the disclosure gate refuses,
how the load is verified.

**Still true, and still the open question:** the README and `docs/investigation.md` §5 describe the

## Stack

Python 3.10+ · [[pandas]] · [[networkx]] · [[streamlit]] · matplotlib · plotly · [[sqlite]] ·
vanilla JS with vendored libraries · [[make]] · ruff · [[pytest]] · [[github-actions]].
~2,200 LOC across eight modules in `src/`.

**[[pandas]] is a presentation dependency here, not a pipeline one.** It is imported by `src/app.py`
and the notebook only; the anonymisation pipeline, the [[disclosure-gate]] and the whole test suite
run on stdlib `csv`. The part that must be trustworthy has the fewest dependencies — the same
instinct as [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]], applied to the Python half.

## Three ways in

| Surface | What it is | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [[streamlit]] dashboard | `src/app.py`, five tabs, `@st.cache_data` | the anomaly console |
| Notebook | `notebooks/01_investigation_analysis.ipynb`, 17 cells | executed headless in CI |
| Static viewer | `interactive/`, 809-line `app.js`, all six JS libs vendored | [[offline-first-static-deliverable]] · [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] |

The zero-dependency path is a deliberate **second** entry point, not the whole project — the
analysis half needs twelve pip packages. `serve.py` is 60 lines of stdlib `http.server`.

## The privacy pipeline

Private source CSVs (outside the repo) plus a git-ignored local rules module feed `anonymize.py`,
which writes `data/` and a git-ignored re-identification mapping. Every value is replaced; every
relationship is preserved — [[structure-preserving-anonymisation]]. Substitution is derived from one
committed global seed via a keyed hash, so the same source value maps identically in every table and
in free text: [[deterministic-seeded-substitution]]. Identifiers keep their shape and lose their
validity — [[format-preserving-invalid-identifiers]]. `validate_anonymization.py` runs the
[[disclosure-gate]] before anything ships.

## The analytical method — and what is not in it

Four named signals, stated identically in `docs/investigation.md` §8, the dashboard, the notebook and
the test suite: **bulk sponsorship** (permits per employer per day over a threshold, reinforced by
permit-serial contiguity), **shared-identifier clustering** (contact-address concentration — 66
nominally independent workers collapsing onto two contact points, see
[[shared-identifier-clustering]]), **declared-wage uniformity** (a modal-spike read off a 30-bin
histogram), and **entity succession** (permits migrating predecessor→successor across a year). A
fifth, graph-based signal counts people adjacent to two or more companies as bridges.

The argument is [[convergent-evidence]] — "not a smoking gun, a convergence", "No single one proves
intent" — with a three-tier reliability scheme and [[chain-of-custody]] back to a `document` row for
every claim.

**What is NOT here, stated so no reader assumes it.** No Benford's law. No z-score or IQR outlier
detection. No time-series anomaly model. No significance testing of any kind. No centrality measure —
degree is used only for node sizing. No ghost-employee test as such: the outsized payroll line and
the implausible-age employees are narrative observations, not computed. No duplicate-record detection
as an analytic — the SHA-256 folding of 2,456 originals down to 512 records is a **deduplication step
in ingestion**, not a fraud test. The method is threshold flags, group-bys, value-count concentration
and a graph, argued as convergence.

## Findings

- **The README's CI claim overstates what CI enforces.** `confidence: high`. The README says no value
  identifies a real party, "a claim that is test-verified in CI"; `ci.yml`'s own comment says the leak
  scan and the stem guard **skip on a clean runner** because the private source and rules are absent.
  CI therefore enforces structural integrity plus a regex sweep only. This is the single largest
  prose-vs-artifact gap in the repo. Recorded on [[disclosure-gate]].
- **Residual source-signalling survives in committed code**, and it contradicts `docs/methodology.md`
  §4's claim that no origin-signalling scrap survives. The `pesel`, `nip`, `regon` and `krs` column
  names carry through DDL, CSV headers, the dashboard and the generated data dictionary; the
  validator's `ALLOW` set contains `"poland"` and `"polish"`; one PII pattern is a `+880` phone
  regex; the viewer still formats numbers with a `pl-PL` locale. None is a person-like value, but
  together they narrow the source jurisdiction and the worker-origin corridor. Stated as a limitation
  on [[structure-preserving-anonymisation]].
- **Two analytical signals are regression-tested against anonymisation damage** —
  `test_shared_inbox_pattern_preserved` and `test_bulk_permit_batch_pattern_preserved`. Testing that
  a *finding* survived the privacy pipeline is unusual and real. See [[reproducible-analysis]].
- **Manifest contradictions.** `pyproject.toml` declares `[project]` with `requires-python = ">=3.10"`
  and a py310 lint target but **no `dependencies` key at all**, so `pip install -e .` installs
  nothing; all twelve runtime deps live only in `requirements.txt`. CI pins Python 3.12, so the
  declared 3.10 floor is never tested. `pyvis` is listed with a comment about entity-graph rendering
  and is imported nowhere. `plotly` is grouped under the same comment but is used only by
  [[streamlit]] — the notebook uses matplotlib exclusively. All deps are floor-pinned with no upper
  bound and no lockfile, under a comment claiming reproducibility. See [[setuptools-and-pyproject]]
  and [[documentation-drift]].
- **Generated docs are committed and then diff-gated in CI** —
  [[generated-docs-checked-by-ci-diff]] and [[generated-audit-artifact]].
- **The `Makefile` is the clean-clone contract, and CI restates it instead of calling it.** `make ci`
  is written as the one command a stranger runs after cloning; `ci.yml` re-expresses the same
  sequence as YAML steps. Nothing checks that the two still agree, so the canonical entry point can
  drift from the enforced one silently. See [[make]] and [[github-actions]] — and contrast
  [[verify-the-load-dont-declare-it]], where the same repo does wire the check to the artifact.
- Limits are written into the shipped prose, not into an appendix: a threat-model section, a "what
  the data will not tell you" section, deliberately retained OCR date errors, and the tiered
  reliability scheme. Strongest instance of [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] in the source set.
- Milder [[documentation-drift]]: the README and methodology call it a "four-way" disclosure gate
  while the validator's own docstring says "two independent checks"; the viewer's i18n module still
  advertises two locales after `build_viewer.py::strip_locale` was written to remove one —
  [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]].
